name: Captain Kennedy
role: U.S. Army captain on the mountain
summary: First named tentatively in VN-0006, on top of the mountain: "Left: I think is captain Kennedy from Boston." Later Larry said it without the hedge: "Captain Kennedy, he was from Boston, his mom sent him a telescope." Asked who ran the camp, he answered: "Special Forces ran the camp. Captain Kennedy was in Charge of the camp most of the time." And again: "Kennedy pretty much ran the camp. When he was gone, Lowry ran the camp." Kennedy, he added, was not there that last week. At sick call for the Cambodians and their families, "Captain Kennedy handled the political problems. Me and the medic handled the sick call" (VN-0041). After Larry ran into a bamboo ladder in the dark and was knocked out for hours, "captain Kennedy was standing over me when I came too" (VN-0069).
researchNotes: Recollections: 2026-09-01-phone-who-ran-the-camp, 2026-09-03-phone-kennedy-and-lowry, giscus-vn-0006-c18006884 and -c18260039, giscus-vn-0041-c18308745, giscus-vn-0069-c18307869. Whether the tentative Kennedy of VN-0006 and the Kennedy of the later accounts are one man has not been confirmed, though Larry dropped the hedge on 2026-09-03. A period order of battle names a different officer as the camp's commander of record during the same months (research/people/nui-ba-den-roster-names.md). The difference is left standing: a commander of record and the man experienced as running the place need not be the same, and rotations through this site were constant. The classification does not move on testimony alone. The VN-0023 photograph and the Hawaii film-developing detail rest on his son's paraphrases of 2026-08-15, one of them held; the analysis that tied Kennedy to that patrol was moved on 2026-09-14 to research/people/records-cleanup-2026-09-14.md (the patrol question in the interview guide asks who was on it).
